plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stems carry huge golden-petaled flower heads with dark, seed-packed centers. Fields and garden borders glow with them at the height of the northern summer, and bees crowd the blooms from morning to dusk.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer into early autumn, with peak flowering in July and August
plants.location: Northern Hemisphere temperate regions, including the American Midwest
plants.funFact: What looks like one big flower is really hundreds of tiny florets packed into a head. The florets in the center often spiral in a Fibonacci-style pattern.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In the southern winter, this Australian tree is covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pompoms. The blooms light up bushland and roadsides when most other plants are still quiet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly July to October or November depending on the region
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Each fluffy ball is a cluster of many tiny flowers, and the long stamens give it its fuzzy look.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic, dinner-plate-sized flower head with a crown of pointed pink bracts around a soft, silvery center. It blooms through the cool southern winter and looks like a cross between an artichoke and a sunburst.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter into spring, roughly July to October
plants.location: Fynbos region of the Western Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Protea is South Africa's national flower. The plant belongs to an ancient family that dates back to when the southern continents were joined, and it is adapted to survive periodic wildfires.
